name: The PIT mutation gate: wiring, scoping, and how to read it
description: Shipped 2026-08-18 (ENGINEERING-BACKLOG item 1), REPORT-ONLY, no threshold. Run with ./gradlew mutationTest (~1m20s warm, six modules); it is deliberately NOT wired into build or check. WIRING: a plain JavaExec on PIT's own CLI entry point (org.pitest.mutationtest.commandline.MutationCoverageReport) in the root build, using the publishableJarModules allow-list idiom -- NOT the info.solidsoft.pitest Gradle plugin, which last shipped 2023-09 and cannot apply on Gradle 9 at all (it reads ReportingExtension.baseDir, removed in Gradle 9); every plugin-portal alternative is staler or Android-specific. The CLI route also lets the engine track its own current line, which matters because only PIT 1.20+ with ASM 9.10.1 reads Java 25 class files. SCOPING: opa-abac-spring-data and example-catalog-management-service restrict --targetTests to *Test, because PIT re-runs the selected tests ONCE PER MUTANT and a Testcontainers IT in that loop makes the run unusable. Consequence: a class exercised only by an IT reports NO_COVERAGE, not untested. HOW TO READ IT: SURVIVED is the signal (a test executed that line and did not notice the code changed); the headline mutation score inherits the scoping distortion, so use test strength instead. BASELINE: 1668 mutations, 1123 killed, 98 survived, test strength 83-94% per module. DO NOT gate on a repo-wide score -- the spread is narrow enough that any threshold either proves nothing or fails a module for a scoping artifact. Full record: docs/code-review/MUTATION-TESTING-BASELINE-2026-08-18.md

PIT died with java.lang.IllegalArgumentException: Unsupported class file major version 69 in org.objectweb.asm.ClassReader, but only on opa-abac-spring-data and example-catalog-management-service -- opa-abac-core and opa-abac-spring-security ran clean on the identical Java 25 bytecode. Major version 69 is Java 25. The cause is classpath ORDER, not a PIT limitation: Spring Boot's test starter drags ASM 9.7.1 in transitively (spring-boot-starter-test -> json-path -> json-smart -> accessors-smart), 9.7.1 reads class files only up to Java 24, and PIT uses a plain UNSHADED org.objectweb.asm.ClassReader -- so whichever ASM is first on the classpath wins. The two library modules never hit it because neither pulls Boot's test starter. This is silent and order-dependent: the same wiring works or dies depending on one module's test dependencies.
resolution: Put the pitest configuration FIRST in the JavaExec classpath, ahead of main output, test output and testRuntimeClasspath, so PIT's own ASM 9.10.1 wins. Diagnose this class of conflict with dependencyInsight --dependency g:a --configuration <cfg>, which prints the RESOLVED winner; the dependency tree shows requested versions and will mislead you.
